provenance.paper: Of Human Criteria and Automatic Metrics: A Benchmark of the Evaluation of Story Generation
provenance.anchor_transcription: Verbatim Table 7 anchor text, without numeric labels; original punctuation retained.

protocol.aggregation: Arithmetic mean separately for each dimension; no aggregate score.
protocol.calibration: Workers were shown the human story alongside the subject story to calibrate their judgment.
protocol.screening: Amazon Mechanical Turk Masters workers in the UK, US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand; judgments under 30 seconds rejected; first-mentioned fictional character name requested.
protocol.prompt_mismatch: Note: if the story is not relevant with respect to the prompt, it only affects the Relevance criterion! Do not rate 1 everywhere, or we will reject!
protocol.unfinished_sentence: Note: some stories have been abruptly cut in the middle of a sentence. Please rate them as if they ended just before the unfinished sentence.
protocol.scope: HANNA-derived human assessment of supplied narratives, not the original dataset or an automated HANNA metric. Missing ratings remain null. Protocol compliance is not verified.

coherence.description: measures whether the story makes sense

anchors.1: The story does not make sense at all. For instance, the setting and/or characters keep changing, and/or there is no understandable plot.
anchors.2: Most of the story does not make sense.
anchors.3: The story mostly makes sense but has some incoherences.
anchors.4: The story almost makes sense overall, except for one or two small incoherences.
anchors.5: The story makes sense from beginning to end.

relevance.description: measures how well the story matches its prompt

anchors.1: The story has no relationship with the prompt at all.
anchors.2: The story only has a weak relationship with the prompt.
anchors.3: The story roughly matches the prompt.
anchors.4: The story matches the prompt, except for one or two small aspects.
anchors.5: The story matches the prompt exactly.

empathy.description: measures how well you understood the characters’ emotions (regardless of whether you agreed with them)

anchors.1: The characters seemed apathetic to you.
anchors.2: At least one character slightly related to you on an emotional level.
anchors.3: You recognized specific, but not necessarily strong, emotions (eg sadness, joy, fear…) in at least one character.
anchors.4: At least one character emotionally involved you, but minor details prevented you from completely relating to them.
anchors.5: At least one character completely involved you on an emotional level.

surprise.description: measures how surprising the end of the story was

anchors.1: The ending seemed completely obvious from the start, or doesn’t make any sense at all.
anchors.2: The ending was easily predictable after a few sentences.
anchors.3: The ending was predictable after half of the story.
anchors.4: The ending surprised you, but would have been difficult to predict.
anchors.5: The ending surprised you, and still seemed as if it could very reasonably have been predicted, ie, there were enough clues in the story.

engagement.description: measures how much you engaged with the story

anchors.1: You found the story boring and were glad it was over.
anchors.2: You found one or two things interesting in the story, but no more.
anchors.4: The story almost kept you engaged until the end.
anchors.5: You were so engaged that you wished there was a sequel.

complexity.description: measures how elaborate the story is

anchors.1: The setting of the story is extremely simple; it only involves one or two characters or concepts.
anchors.2: The setting of the story is simple; one or two characters, a simple plot, maybe an indication of time or location.
anchors.3: The story is somewhat developed: it involves at least one of the following: complex concepts, realistic characters, an intricate plot, an underlying history or circumstances, precise descriptions.
anchors.4: The story is developed: it involves at least two of the following: complex concepts, realistic characters, an intricate plot, an underlying history or circumstances, precise descriptions.
anchors.5: The story is well thought-out: it involves at least three of the following: complex concepts, realistic characters, an intricate plot, an underlying history or circumstances, precise descriptions.
